title: So Juno 1 — opening bass reconstruction
method: Hardware-only low-frequency peaks, octave-spaced harmonic families, and amplitude discontinuities identify five opening events. The lower sine and Upper square both sound one octave below the played key; the Upper saw sounds at the played key. The two low E-flat events therefore map to MIDI 39, the octave-up E-flat events to 51, and the final D-flat to 49. The crop stops before the later continuous pitch movement. No Septum rendering was consulted to derive notes or times.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable; this is a source-audio reconstruction, not a recovered original performance.
All velocities are fixed to 100 as an explicit unknown placeholder; no velocity, preset parameter, or recording EQ was fitted to Septum output.

Played-note inference assumes default system transpose and the documented/current WIDE-dependent oscillator ranges. Original system settings, controller events, exact recorded patch revision, and recording processing are unknown.
Event times refer to decoded MP3 audio. Hardware latency, encoder history, oscillator state, and effect history are not recovered; no post-render alignment or time warping is implied.
Onsets and abrupt note-offs are approximate within 10–20 ms; an octave transition may contain a small overlap that cannot be recovered.
The final note is cropped while still sounding. Its note-off at 1.55 seconds is an artificial boundary, not a measured hardware release.
The published delay remains enabled. Earlier-note echoes and small pitch drift remain in the hardware excerpt.

published_tuning_audit: DUAL, octave shift 0 for both tones. Upper saw raw coarse 64/WIDE off → 0; Upper square 52/WIDE on → −12; Lower sine 28/WIDE off → −12. Arpeggiator off; both portamento switches off. Upper SOLO, Lower POLY. Delay on, reverb off.
